title: Aleister Crowley: Blowhard Narcissist?
summary: Josh and Chuck profile occultist Aleister Crowley (1875-1947), covering his wealthy, strictly religious childhood in England and the Plymouth Brethren, his time at Cambridge, mountaineering (including a failed K2 attempt and an avalanche tragedy), poetry, bisexuality and sex magic, his marriage to Rose Kelly and the Book of the Law, founding Thelema, joining the Golden Dawn and the O.T.O., his lawsuit and espionage claims, his heroin addiction and death, and his lasting influence on the 1960s counterculture, the Sergeant Pepper cover, and the New Age movement. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about stickers left at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
topics: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn

segments.title: Opening banter and Crowley's reputation
segments.summary: The hosts explain the show's title, then discuss Crowley's divisive reputation, his perceived narcissism, and why he is worth an episode.

segments.title: Who Crowley was and his childhood
segments.summary: Introduction to Crowley's image and influence on occultism, then his birth in 1875 England to a wealthy family of brewers who belonged to the Plymouth Brethren. His father died of cancer after refusing medical treatment, which the hosts say soured Crowley on Christianity.

segments.title: Cambridge, mountaineering, and chess
segments.summary: Crowley's time at Cambridge, where he became interested in the occult and sex. He was a chess player, a mountaineer on a British attempt on K2, and eventually gave up climbing for magic and sex.

segments.title: Poetry and Celia Farts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Crowley's erotic poetry, including White Stains published under the pseudonym Archibald Bishop, and the crude poem Celia Farts, which they say shows his attitude toward his writing.

segments.title: Sexuality, manipulation, and acolytes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Crowley's sexual experiences, including a mystical experience tied to a first homosexual encounter in Stockholm, his bisexuality and relationship with Jerome Pauli, and how he used sexual degradation and wealth to dominate followers. They note the accusations against him are hard to verify.

segments.title: Golden Dawn, O.T.O., and the Boleskine House
segments.summary: Crowley's travels, his entry into the Golden Dawn and the O.T.O., his rivalry with W.B. Yeats, who reportedly sicked a vampire on him, and his Boleskine House on Loch Ness, later owned by Jimmy Page.

segments.title: Marriage to Rose, the Book of the Law, and family tragedies
segments.summary: Crowley's 1903 marriage to Rose Kelly, their 1904 Cairo honeymoon where he said he received the Book of the Law from a being called Aiwass, and the death of their daughter Lilith in Burma. The hosts discuss his blame of Rose, his mountaineering expedition tragedy, and Rose's institutionalization.

segments.title: Thelema, sex magic, and the Sicily abbey
segments.summary: The hosts describe Crowley's Thelema, his rented farmhouse Abbey of Thelema in Sicily where extreme rituals reportedly took place, and his view of magic as a middle ground between science and religion. They also discuss the law 'Do what thou wilt' and how it was misinterpreted.

segments.title: Later life, espionage claims, death, and legacy
segments.summary: Crowley's lawsuit over O.T.O. secrets, his claimed spying for Britain and Germany during the wars, his travels, heroin addiction after a doctor prescribed it, and his death in 1947. The hosts cover his later fame, the Sgt. Pepper cover, the New Age movement, and claims linking L. Ron Hubbard and Jack Parsons to his followers.

segments.title: Closing and listener mail
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh mention a planned short stuff episode on Crowley's son, then read a listener mail about stickers placed at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and sign off.
